items.title: The internet needs a nap (and you do, too)
items.summary: Bill takes a break from the non-stop breaking news to promote prioritizing environmental awareness and team stability over reactive patching.

items.title: The challenge of defending against bulletproof dead drops on public blockchains
items.summary: The evolution of malware command-and-control (C2) infrastructure has shifted away from fragile, centralized servers and hardcoded domains toward resilient, decentralized blockchain networks that eliminate single points of failure.

items.title: UAT-12643: Suspected North Korea-aligned actor blends blockchain resilience with targeted infostealing
items.summary: Cisco Talos discovered malicious infrastructure associated with a financially motivated threat group we are tracking as UAT-12643.

items.title: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java
items.summary: Cisco Talos is tracking the disclosure of a critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed “Java4Shell,” with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 that may lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).

items.title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
items.summary: AI-enabled penetration testing and red team frameworks can automate and chain reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow-on actions, lowering the skill threshold for attackers and accelerating intrusions when the tools are misused.

items.title: Never be afraid to ask questions
items.summary: Amy reflects on a formative college anthropology course that taught her the power of asking questions to bridge cultural gaps.

items.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for November 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities
items.summary:
Microsoft has released its monthly security update for November 2026, which includes 1095 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 64 that Microsoft marked as "critical."
Out of 64 "critical" vulnerabilities, 48 are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.

items.title: Bring a tent, I've got the coffee: Lessons from it-sa
items.summary: Thorsten may have had to camp out in Nuremberg to attend it-sa, but the real story is the initiative to add a formal IT Security apprenticeship program in Germany for the thousands of young hackers ready to join our side.

items.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
items.summary: The self-deleting VOLTA infostealer steals credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Then, it uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.

items.title: A quiet week in infosec <.<
items.summary: In this edition of the Threat Source newsletter, William explores how PHP has taken over the conversation, Node.js has joined in, but underneath it all, there are still good people doing good work.

items.title: IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases
items.summary: Phishing remained the leading initial access technique, while percentage of ransomware and pre-ransomware cases increased. Finance and public administration tied as the top-targeted industries.

items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.summary: Cisco Talos observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework in the wild called “NIK C2.”
